newsitem.title: USA: Cuban lawmakers in U.S. seek to isolate Castro.
newsitem.headline: Cuban lawmakers in U.S. seek to isolate Castro.

text.p: Cuban-American members of Congress met with Latin American and Caribbean diplomats on Thursday to urge their countries not to trade with Cuba while Fidel Castro remains in power.

The meeting was held by Florida Republican Representative Ileana Ros-Lehtinen one day after she introduced a bill in the House of Representatives proposing the suspension of economic aid to Caribbean nations that back Cuba's membership of CARICOM.
Her bill also proposed denying U.S. tariff benefits to imports from any Caribbean basin country that negotiates a free trade agreemeent with Cuba.

"It is clear that to trade with a dictatorship such as the Castro regime not only makes poor economic sense but goes against every moral and philosophical belief that we, as democratic governments, are committed to promoting and safeguarding," she told the diplomats.
President Castro's government proposed joining the Caribbean Community two years ago, but CARICOM has been dragging its feet, fearing it might anger Washington.

At last month's CARICOM summit in Montego Bay, Jamaica, Caribbean leaders once again postponed a decision on whether to negotiate a free trade accord with Cuba. Diplomatic sources cited "political considerations" for the new delay.

"There should be some restriction on Cuba to come into the mainstream," Bahamas Ambassador Sir Arlington Butler told Reuters. "CARICOM is sympathetic to the people of Cuba because they live in poverty."

Florida Republican Representative Lincoln Diaz-Balart criticised some of the hemisphere's countries for adopting a double standard on Cuba by wanting economic freedom to trade with a country where there was no political freedom.

He said Congress would be reluctant to grant the Clinton administration a "blank check" and authorise speeded up neotiation of free trade throughout the Americas if political rights were not taken into account.
"There is dissatisfaction with the double standard we see in our hemisphere toward this brutal dictatorship and this double standard is totally unacceptable," Diaz-Balart said.
Latin American nations and Canada have opposed U.S. efforts to discourage foreign investment in Cuba by tightening a 35-year-old economic embargo on the Communist-ruled island.
